verses.text: Then fourteen years later I went up to Jerusalem again with Barnabas. I took Titus with me too.
I went because God showed me I should. I explained to them the Good News I preach among the Gentiles. I did this in private with the leaders, so that my work would not be wasted, now or before.
Titus was with me. He was a Greek, but even he was not forced to be circumcised.
This matter came up because of some false believers. They had sneaked in to spy on the freedom we have in Christ Jesus. They wanted to make us slaves again.
We did not give in to them, not even for a moment. We wanted the truth of the Good News to stay with you.
Those who seemed to be important added nothing to my message. What they once were makes no difference to me. God does not judge by how people look.
Instead, they saw that God had trusted me with the Good News for the Gentiles, just as he had trusted Peter with it for the Jews.
God was at work in Peter as an apostle to the Jews. He was also at work in me as an apostle to the Gentiles.

James, Peter and John were seen as pillars of the church. They saw the grace God had given me. So they shook hands with Barnabas and me as partners. They agreed that we should go to the Gentiles, and they would go to the Jews.
They only asked us to keep remembering the poor. That was the very thing I was keen to do.
But when Peter came to Antioch, I stood up to him face to face, because he was clearly wrong.
Before some men came from James, Peter used to eat with the Gentiles. But when they came, he drew back and kept apart. He was afraid of those who wanted Gentiles to be circumcised.
The other Jewish believers joined him in this pretending. Even Barnabas was led astray by it.

I saw that they were not living by the truth of the Good News. So I said to Peter in front of them all, "You are a Jew, yet you live like a Gentile and not like a Jew. So how can you force Gentiles to live like Jews?
"We were born Jews, and not Gentile sinners.

Yet we know that a person is not made right with God by keeping the law. It is through faith in Jesus Christ. So we too put our faith in Christ Jesus, to be made right with God by faith in Christ, and not by keeping the law. No one will be made right with God by keeping the law.
We look to Christ to make us right with God. But what if we are then found to be sinners? Does that mean Christ helps us to sin? Certainly not!
If I build again what I tore down, I show that I am a law-breaker.
Through the law I died to the law, so that I can live for God.
I have been crucified with Christ. It is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me. The life I now live in this body, I live by faith in the Son of God. He loved me and gave himself for me.
I do not set aside the grace of God. If we could be made right with God through the law, then Christ died for nothing!"
